findings.evidence:
S: I checked the published alt at site MDX:78 clause by clause. It is identical to inventory item 1 and to draft/.rounds/8.json '[published] alt:jh-3-contributions.png' (both compared by script, True), and it is the render of gate.toml:74. The only difference from 7.json is that ' on wages up to a ceiling' was deleted after JP's '3 percent'. Nothing was added. (a) 'Bar chart of contribution rates each year, worker and employer': I opened charts/jh-3-contributions.png. Its title reads 'Contribution rates each year, worker and employer', the axis reads 'Contribution rate, percent', and it has worker and employer stacks (make_charts.py:165-166). (b) CPF '37 percent for workers aged 55 and under, on wages in the top band': my script summed data/cpf_contribution_rates.csv (sha256 c4529a8e..., matching data/README.md:111). 2026-01 is the last effective_from. The rows at lines 668-675 give Employer 17 + Employee 20 = 37.0 for '35 years & below', 'Above 35 - 45', 'Above 45 - 50' and 'Above 50 - 55'. 'Above 55 - 60' is 34.0, so the edge at 55 is right. The stored dataset description, sources/provenance/cpf/meta_d_98ffa142ae0dec40391f78f81d26aca9.json (sha256 26daef4b...), says 'The CPF contribution rates are applicable for the highest wage band', which supports 'top band'. results.json gives cpf 20/17/37, max_age 55. (c) 401(k) '12.1 percent on average among participants in 2024' in 'plans Vanguard keeps records for': vanguard_how_america_saves_2026.txt (sha256 34b506ce..., matching sources.json) :224, 'Average total contribution rate (participant and employer) Figure 44 11.6% 11.7% 12.0% 12.1% 12.1%*', under the column header at :184 (2021 to 2025). 2024 = 12.1 with no asterisk; the asterisk marks 2025 only (:234). :2565-2566 says 'These rates exclude eligible nonparticipants', which supports 'among participants'. The Methodology at :6662-6664, 'plans ... for which Vanguard directly provides recordkeeping services', supports the plan phrase. (d) 'JHT, 5.7 percent': PP 46/2015 Pasal 16(1), pp_46_2015.txt (sha256 8345590b..., matching sources.json), 'sebesar 5,7% (lima koma tujuh persen) dari Upah' with 2% worker and 3.7% employer. (e) 'JP, a separate pension, 3 percent': PP 45/2015 Pasal 28(2), pp_45_2015.txt (sha256 995c021e..., matching sources.json), 'sebesar 3% (tiga persen) dari Upah per bulan', split 2% employer and 1% worker in Pasal 28(3). After the deletion, the JP clause is a plain rate like every other clause under the 'contribution rates' lead-in. The rate stays 3% even where the Pasal 29(2) wage cap binds, because the cap limits the wage base, not the rate. So the alt implies no ceiling for JP and none for CPF. JP's ceiling is still stated in the post at draft .md:13 and MDX:22. Notes, not defects, all predating round 7: the CPF clause leaves out the dataset's sector scope ('private sector employees and public sector non-pensionable employees'); the JHT 5.7 split applies to employers other than state organs, which the post's .md:13 says; 'each year' beside 'rates' is redundant (round 7 style note); and How America Saves' universe is 'Vanguard defined contribution plans permitting employee-elective deferrals', which the alt labels 'a 401(k)'. | L: Published alt at site MDX:78 is identical to the inventory text (lens-L/cmp.py printed 'alt==item1: True'), and it renders from gate.toml:74. Each clause checked as a rate under the 'contribution rates' lead-in: (a) CPF 37, aged 55 and under, top band. The stored metadata (sources/provenance/cpf/meta_d_98ffa142...json) says 'As a proportion of wage ... The CPF contribution rates are applicable for the highest wage band ... wages of $750 or more per month'; results.json contributions.cpf has total_pct 37.0 and max_age 55. (b) 401(k) 12.1 'on average among participants in 2024': results.json k401 has total_pct 12.1 and year 2024, and HAS :224 was verified in round 7. It is an average rate and the alt says 'on average'. (c) JHT 5.7: PP 46/2015 Pasal 16(1), pp_46_2015.txt:428-434. (d) JP 3: PP 45/2015 Pasal 28(2), pp_45_2015.txt:822-823 ('3% (tiga persen) dari Upah per bulan'). With no ceiling clause, the alt holds as rates: BPJS's own tariff table (bpjs_ir_2025.txt:3318-3326) gives JP as '3% dari upah sebulan (dengan batas upah atas tahun 2025 sebesar Rp10.547.400 ...)', so the rate and the ceiling are stated separately. CPF Board's metadata uses the same structure. JP and CPF are now treated alike: neither mentions a ceiling. CPF's 'on wages in the top band' is the dataset's lower-band qualifier ('$750 or more'), not a ceiling, and JP has no lower band (Pasal 28(2) sets a flat 3%), so the remaining asymmetry says nothing about ceilings. Notes, not defects: 'each year' is carried over from round 6 (style, already noted in round 7). findings.evidence: S: The chart 3 note, MDX:79-83 figcaption, matches the make_charts.py:170-177 footnote rendered with results.json values, after whitespace normalisation. It also matches inventory item 2 (script: True for both). I opened charts/jh-3-contributions.png and the note shows with no 'ceiling'. The PNG has sha256 60b288b7..., the same in charts/, site public/images/blog/ and the .docx word/media/image3.png. Clause by clause: (1) 'JHT and JP: the rates the regulations set (PP 46/2015 Pasal 16; PP 45/2015 Pasal 28)': Pasal 16(1) sets 5.7% (2 worker + 3.7 employer), and Pasal 28(2)-(3) sets 3% (1 worker + 2 employer). Both are Peraturan Pemerintah, and the chart's stacks match (results.json jht 2/3.7, jp 1/2). Both cites map to reference entries 2015b and 2015a (draft .md:137, :135). (2) '401(k): Vanguard, How America Saves 2026, plans Vanguard keeps records for, 2024, among participants: the average deferral rate as the worker share, and the average total contribution rate less that as the employer share (a difference of two averages)': HAS :214 gives 'Average participant deferral rate ... 7.6%' for 2024 and :224 gives 12.1% for 2024. results.json k401 employer 4.5 = 12.1 - 7.6 (recomputed). :2566 'These rates exclude eligible nonparticipants'; Methodology :6662-6664 covers the recordkeeping universe. The citation maps to Vanguard 2026a (.md:155). (3) '401(k) deferrals are optional': unchanged since round 6. It is consistent with HAS's voluntary and automatic enrollment with opt-out, and with the post's 'The 401(k) is voluntary'. (4) 'CPF: CPF Board contribution rates in force on 1 January 2026 for wages in the top band, the same for each age group up to 55': the CSV's last effective_from is '2026-01', and the four groups up to 55 each have Employer 17 and Employee 20. The meta says 'highest wage band'. data.gov.sg and the licence URL https://data.gov.sg/open-data-licence match data/README.md:101-106,125. The reference entry is Central Provident Fund Board 2026 (.md:119). (5) 'JP is a separate pension scheme': PP 45/2015 governs Jaminan Pensiun, separate from PP 46/2015 (JHT). The round 7 deletion removed the clause ', and its rate applies to wages up to a ceiling'. That left a note in which no clause is now uncited or miscited: the earlier round 7 note, that the note cited Pasal 28 while the ceiling sits in Pasal 29, is moot now that the ceiling clause is gone. (6) 'Calculations by the author': the 4.5 employer share and the CPF 37 sum are derived values. All of this was confirmed by my recomputation in lens-S/cmp.py. | L: With whitespace normalised, the site MDX:79-83 figcaption equals the inventory text (cmp.py: 'figcaption==item2: True'). make_charts.py no longer contains 'ceiling' (cmp.py: False), and its footnote at :171-177 matches. I opened the PNG and its note reads word for word the same. The site PNG and charts/jh-3-contributions.png share sha1 d72b63b2e245f80e05de82f83a7469af227ddc18. The round 7 change was deleting ', and its rate applies to wages up to a ceiling' from 'JP is a separate pension scheme' (round7-verdicts.json r7:item:5 quotes the old wording). Clauses as rates: 'JHT and JP: the rates the regulations set (PP 46/2015 Pasal 16; PP 45/2015 Pasal 28)'. Pasal 16(1) gives 5.7 = 2 + 3.7 (pp_46_2015.txt:428-434), and Pasal 28(2)-(3) gives 3 = 1 + 2 (pp_45_2015.txt:820-832). BPJS IR 2025 shows both still in force in 2025: JHT '5,7% dari upah sebulan' with 2% worker and 3.7% employer (:3296-3301), and JP 3% with 1% worker and 2% employer (:3318-3326). Now that the ceiling sentence is gone, the Pasal 28 citation covers only the rate, so round 7's point that the ceiling sits in the uncited Pasal 29 no longer applies. 'JP is a separate pension scheme' is true: it is a separate programme under PP 45/2015, apart from JHT under PP 46/2015. The 401(k) clause describes averages ('the average deferral rate ... a difference of two averages'). 'Worker share' and 'employer share' name the bar segments, which are defined as rates, not as shares of wages. The CPF clause is a Board rate per the metadata. JP and CPF are treated alike: neither has a ceiling clause. Licence: the deletion left the 'Singapore Open Data Licence, data.gov.sg/open-data-licence' credit and 'Non-commercial use' untouched. Note: Pasal 28(4)-(5) (pp_45_2015.txt:834-841) provides for evaluation and a gradual rise toward 8%. The rate set today is still 3%, as IR 2025 confirms, so 'the rates the regulations set' holds. | K: I rebuilt the note string from make_charts.py:170-177 using results.json (k401 year 2024; cpf max_age 55). That string equals the MDX figcaption at :79-83 joined with spaces (True). The figcaption's line breaks also equal textwrap.wrap(note, 150) (True), which matches footnote() at make_charts.py:61-63 (WRAP=150). The opened PNG shows the same five lines, breaking at 'keeps / records', 'as the / employer', 'for wages / in the top band' and 'separate / pension'. To show the PNG comes from the current code, I copied make_charts.py and results.json to lens-K/regen and ran it. The new jh-3-contributions.png has sha256 60b288b7e5be4bb1f3170d384eb9b9ea3d28c65b66bc36c9147e430303c7ff2d, the same as charts/, site public/images/blog/jh-3-contributions.png and the .docx word/media/image3.png, and a PIL pixel diff gives bbox None. Content checks: PP 46/2015 Pasal 16 (pp_46_2015.txt:426-434) gives 5.7% = 2% worker + 3.7% employer. PP 45/2015 Pasal 28 (pp_45_2015.txt:820-833) gives 3% = 1% worker + 2% employer. Vanguard's average total contribution rate is 12.1% in 2024 (vanguard_how_america_saves_2026.txt:224). The CPF rows for 2026-01 are 20 (Employee) / 17 (Employer) for all four age groups from '35 years & below' to 'Above 50 - 55 years' (data/cpf_contribution_rates.csv), which supports 'the same for each age group up to 55'. The word 'ceiling' does not appear in the note, PNG or figcaption. The note agrees with the alt and with the prose at MDX:22 and :86.

findings.evidence: L: A5's new bullet is at design doc :143. These parts hold. (1) 'chart 3's title, axis, labels, note and alt text give rates': title 'Contribution rates each year, worker and employer' (make_charts.py:166, PNG opened); axis 'Contribution rate, percent' (:165); value labels f"{total_pct:g}%" (:160), which the PNG shows as 37%, 12.1%, 5.7%, 3%; the note says 'the rates the regulations set', 'average deferral rate', 'average total contribution rate' and 'CPF Board contribution rates'; the alt text is MDX:78 'Bar chart of contribution rates ...' and draft .md:50 'Contribution rates each year, worker and employer'. (2) 'the post states JP's wage ceiling in its prose only': 'ceiling' appears once in the draft (.md:13) and once in the MDX (:22, the same prose sentence; cmp.py found one occurrence, at offset 2296). It appears 0 times in make_charts.py and in the gate.toml alt templates, and grep finds it in neither README.md nor data/README.md. (3) The dates: rounds.jsonl shows round 6 closed at 2026-10-24T00:37Z and round 7 at 01:04Z, which is 20:37 and 21:04 on 2026-10-23 in New York, matching A5's New York dating. The flaw: 'R7's "shares of wages" is shown as the contribution rates the rules set' covers all four of R7's bars, but no rule sets the 401(k) bar. It is Vanguard's average total contribution rate among participants in 2024 (results.json contributions.k401 total_pct 12.1, year 2024). R7 itself calls it 'a typical 401(k) from How America Saves 2026' (design doc :63). Chart 3's own note says 'the average deferral rate ... the average total contribution rate less that ... (a difference of two averages). 401(k) deferrals are optional.' Round 7's lens L also recorded 'That bar is an average of participants' rates, not a rule' (r7:item:4). So A5 misdescribes one of the four bars. The phrase is carried over from the round 6 owner-decision text ('chart 3 and the CPF line describe the contribution rates the rules set'), which was about the JP and CPF ceilings. Applied to all of R7, it overreaches. This is an internal pre-registration record and appears on no reader surface, so severity is LOW. Minor notes, not refuted: 'states JP's wage ceiling' means it states that a ceiling exists, not its value. The A5 header still reads 'after fact-check round 1', but the bullet dates itself 'after rounds 6 and 7'. The header's 'No rule R1 to R8 and no result changes' still holds, because the bullet records a presentation choice and round 7 changed only the alt text, the note and a docstring. | skeptic L: I re-ran the checks myself and the finding stands. (1) Design doc :143 contains the bullet word for word. R7 at :63-64 covers four bars, JHT, JP, 'a typical 401(k) from How America Saves 2026' and CPF, so a phrase about all of R7 covers the 401(k) bar too. (2) No rule sets the 401(k) bar. In results.json, contributions.k401 = {worker_pct 7.6, employer_pct 4.5, total_pct 12.1, year 2024}. Chart 3's note (make_charts.py:171-174) calls these 'among participants: the average deferral rate ... the average total contribution rate less that ... (a difference of two averages). 401(k) deferrals are optional.' The stored source sources/text/vanguard_how_america_saves_2026.txt:224 has the row 'Average total contribution rate (participant and employer)', and :2560-2565 has 'average total participant contribution rate ... These rates exclude eligible nonparticipants.' So the bar is a participant average, not a rate set by any rule. JHT and JP are set by regulation (note: 'the rates the regulations set (PP 46/2015 Pasal 16; PP 45/2015 Pasal 28)'), and CPF uses the CPF Board's rates. (3) Where the phrase came from: round6-verdicts.json records the owner-decision fix as 'chart 3 and the CPF line describe the contribution rates the rules set, which hold above a wage ceiling.' That decision was about the JP and CPF ceilings. A5 widens the wording to cover all of R7. Round 7 lens L already noted 'That bar is an average of participants' rates, not a rule' (round7-verdicts.json). (4) The other parts of the bullet hold. Title 'Contribution rates each year, worker and employer' and axis 'Contribution rate, percent' are at make_charts.py:165-166, and the bar labels are f"{total_pct:g}%". 'ceiling' appears once in the draft (.md:13) and once in the MDX (offset 2296, the same prose sentence). It appears 0 times in make_charts.py and gate.toml. round7_fixes.txt confirms that JP's 'up to a ceiling' was removed from chart 3's alt text and note. rounds.jsonl gives round 6 closed at 2026-10-24T00:37Z and round 7 at 01:04Z, which is 2026-10-23 in New York. (5) Severity LOW is right. The text is an internal record in the design doc and appears on no reader surface. One side note outside this finding: HAS :459-464 and :2560-2561 give 7.6% and 12.1% for 2025 (12.1 marked estimated), while results.json labels these 2024. The :224 row also shows 12.1 for the year before. Another lens may want to look at the deferral-year pairing.

findings.evidence: Quoted from design doc A5 at docs/2026-10-21-jht-401k-design.md:143: "R7's 'shares of wages' is shown as the contribution rates the rules set (owner decision, 2026-10-23, after rounds 6 and 7): chart 3's title, axis, labels, note and alt text give rates, and the post states JP's wage ceiling in its prose only." The second clause checks out on every surface: title :166, axis :165, '%' labels :160, note :170-177, alt gate.toml:74 / MDX:78, and JP's ceiling appears only in the MDX:22 prose. R7 (design doc :63-65) covers all four bars, though. One of them, the 401(k), is not a rate any rule sets: the chart note calls it Vanguard's 'average deferral rate' and 'average total contribution rate ... (a difference of two averages)'. The round 6 owner decision this records was about JP and CPF. So 'the contribution rates the rules set' is wrong for one of the four bars. This is an internal record only, and no published surface says it. | skeptic: I re-checked this against the files. docs/2026-10-21-jht-401k-design.md:63-65 (R7) and :73 (chart 3) put all four bars under R7: JHT, JP, a typical 401(k) and CPF. For the 401(k) bar, no rule sets the rate. make_charts.py:170-177 (chart 3 note) builds it from Vanguard's 'average deferral rate' as the worker share and 'the average total contribution rate less that' as the employer share ('a difference of two averages'), and the note adds '401(k) deferrals are optional.' gate.toml:74 (chart 3 alt) says the same: '12.1 percent on average among participants in 2024'. Design doc A2 (:114-117) records this as a choice of survey year, not a statutory rate. Only JHT and JP ('the rates the regulations set', PP 46/2015 Pasal 16; PP 45/2015 Pasal 28) and CPF (CPF Board rates in force on 1 January 2026) are rates set by rules. So the most natural reading, 'rates the rules set', is wrong for one of the four bars. One other reading exists: elsewhere this doc uses 'the rules' for its own R1 to R8 (section 4 heading :47; :122 'which the rules left open'). Under that reading the phrase would be circular, because A5 is restating what R7 shows, and it would still be ambiguous. Either way the bullet is unclear or overstated. The finding's second clause holds: title make_charts.py:166 and axis :165 give rates, the bar labels at :160 are '%', the alt is gate.toml:74, and the post's JP ceiling appears in draft .md:13 prose and is gone from the chart note. The finding's 'internal record only' is also correct: grep finds 'rules set' only at design doc :143, in no draft or gate file. LOW severity.
